title: 100th Floor Boss
text: “How should I put this… it’s like an instant replay of Motoyasu-kun right after the loop, huh?”
“…I hope an Usaunny-type shows up next.”
“Should I be relieved we’re past the Peckul corner?”
Ren and Father arrived a bit behind Itsuki, indeed. What came out next was an Inult Shadow-type, but our winning streak showed no signs of stopping, I say!
“Behold, Dark Wake Legend and Rafumi Murder!”
I shouted as a Brave Inult Shadow and a Lightning Unicorn appeared, and I finished them off with Earth Ignition X, indeed.
“Motoyasu, is that a move name? Are you deliberately one-shotting them with fake-sounding battle cries?”
Ren pointed his sword at me the same way Itsuki had earlier. Whatever did he mean by that, I wonder?
“Dark Awakening Legend… and Rafumi-chan Murder, was it…”
“The fact that it’s premeditated, and there’s not even the hesitation he showed with the Brave Peckul Shadow — I feel some serious malice there.”
“And ‘Murder’ in the first place is just—”
“Motoyasu-kun. I get that it looks like Ren, but shouting out whatever’s on your mind while gutting it without hesitation is a bit much, don’t you think—?”
“It was unavoidable in order to press forward, I say. Besides, if we got mixed up in the chaos and mistook it for the real thing, that would be a disaster.”
“Sure, sure…”
“I’d appreciate it if you understood that mistaking someone for a monster is rather rude.”

For some reason, Ren and Itsuki were being unusually chatty with each other. Unavoidable in order to press forward, indeed. Having already defeated a Peckul wielding a shield modeled after Father, we had no choice but to keep going.
“At this rate, an Usaunny Shadow should show up next, but…”
“Leave it to me.”
“This is our turn to shine. We can mow these down easily now. Let’s show them what the Bow Hero can really do — a proper rabbit hunt!”

Itsuki and Ren, looking oddly fired up, made quick work of the Usaunny Shadows as we advanced. What appeared afterward was a Cloud Naga and a Brave Usaunny Shadow. I couldn’t very well lose to them either, I say!
“Brionac X, indeed!”
“Pyo—”
And thus the Cloud Naga and Brave Usaunny Shadow were annihilated, indeed.
“Whoa… this guy just vaporized a monster that looks a lot like himself without even hesitating…”
“Hahaha! An Usaunny Shadow is basically the same as an Usapil, which is Filolial-sama’s feed, indeed!”
“I don’t think ‘they’re both rabbit-related’ really justifies mowing it down that casually, though—”
“Doesn’t it feel weird to you, Motoyasu, killing something that looks just like yourself?”

Not in the slightest, I say. It was nothing more than a cheap imitation of me. Striking it down with Brionac felt like putting my own foolish past self out of its misery. Don’t lump it together with monsters that resemble Father, I say.
“In a way, maybe that’s something worth learning from…?”
“I’m getting sick of this. The top floor’s probably close now. Let’s move.”
We reached the 100th floor. What emerged was a dragon of unusually massive build that, for some reason, brought to mind Rival’s baby dragon form. Its name was A Bao A Qu, indeed.
“GAOOOOOOOOOON!”
It let out a cry that sounded distinctly Rival-esque, indeed.
“Quite the comical dragon to show up on the 100th floor. It’s like fighting Rival — gives me a real sense of purpose, I say!”

“Does it really look that much like Gaelion-chan? I mean, sure, it’s dragon-type, but going by the name, I think it’s supposed to be a phantom beast rather than a proper dragon — I don’t recall any ‘dragon’ classification for it, though.”
“I wouldn’t say it looks that similar.”
“In my world, it’s famous as a fortress that shows up in a robot anime. Though the original source material for that probably traces back to a phantom beast too.”
“A phantom beast, huh… Being the 100th floor boss, I doubt we can talk it down, can we?”
“GAOOOOOOOOON!”

Crackle-crackle! A Bao A Qu unleashed a lightning breath straight at us, clearly with zero intention of having a conversation, indeed. Father stepped forward and deployed his Shooting Star Shield to block it.
“GAOOOOOOOOOON!”
“If only Rival would say ‘The true mastermind is Gaelion-noooon!’ right about now, this would be perfect, indeed.”
“GAOOOOOO! GAA!”

This time, falling rocks came raining down from above, but we handled that easily too, I say. There was also an earthquake attack that shook the ground with a rumbling boom, but it posed no real threat against our power, indeed.
“It’s not showing any sign of doing that, though.”
“This is Rival’s revenge for hiding a broken heart, I say. Surely.”
“It’s more like Motoyasu-kun wants to pin everything on Gaelion-chan no matter what. Gaelion-chan does love a good bit, but she’s actually quite reserved when it comes to romance.”
“Up until she came back, though, she was sending some pretty resentful vibes Naofumi’s way.”
“True, she has calmed down quite a bit. These days she mostly settles for the same position as Raph-chan, getting petted by Naofumi-san on equal footing.”
That’s exactly its strategy, I say.
“Meeting me here was the end of its luck! Now that its true form is revealed, I shall snuff out its very breath, indeed!”
“I’d say it’s not so much ‘its true form’ as just a different dragon entirely—”
“I’ll finish it in one blow, indeed!”
For my part, since it felt like facing Rival, this was an extremely easy opponent to deal with, I say.

“Then I’ll finish you off in one go, Rival! Take this! Aiming Lancer X! Brionac X! Gungnir X! Liberation Fire Eye X! Liberation Firestorm X! Liberation Prominence X! Hahaha! Weak! Far too weak, aaaaaaaaah!”
“Motoyasu, calm down! There’s such a thing as overkill!”
“Are you trying to destroy this place!?”
“If you break the way back to normal along with everything else, calm down already—!”
Father and the others cheered me on as I unleashed a furious assault upon A Bao A Qu. I wanted them to watch, indeed!
“And this shall be the finishing blow, I say—!”
And with that, I obliterated the giant Rival-esque dragon that was not, in fact, A Bao A Qu at all, indeed.
“S-somehow the dungeon managed to survive intact, it seems.”
“I really wish he’d learn some restraint.”
“Couldn’t agree more.”

Once the smoke covering the 100th floor cleared, Father and the others continued talking. All that remained was to pass through the dungeon-clear door. Incidentally, when I defeated A Bao A Qu, a weapon was unlocked, indeed. It was something called the True Usaunny Spear. It seemed to be a weapon with a special effect that hugely boosted Usaunny-related stats, indeed.
“Ren said the 100th floor boss was supposed to be Abend Great D, but I guess that wasn’t it after all.”
“Yeah. Guess this world really doesn’t play by game knowledge after all.”
“So… I suppose this technically counts as the top floor? That coelacanth model we found along the way… was that just a souvenir, then?”
Incidentally, the coelacanth model was currently in Ren’s possession, indeed. Since it was fairly large, we’d taken to carrying it in turns.
“I really hope it isn’t just that, but…”
“First one to clear it is me, I say—!”
Just as I approached what looked like the goal door… I heard a voice. It sounded remarkably like Filo-tan’s.
“This voice will play back as the voice of whichever member of the opposite sex you hold dearest~”
“Hau!? I hear Filo-tan’s voice! Where is it, I say!?”
“Eh? You hear a voice like that?”
“Do you? Ah, wait, I think I hear something too.”
“Hm? You guys hear something?”
Father and Itsuki cupped their hands to their ears, indeed.

‘Spear Guy, you sure made it far~ But the current you doesn’t have what it takes to open the door up ahead yet~ To open this heavily sealed door, you’ll need keys scattered all across the labyrinth. Apparently you have to gather them together with the friends who challenged the labyrinth with you~ So go back and search each corner of the labyrinth once more for the hidden keys. Also, each island’s labyrinth has handy tools and spells hidden away, so go challenge those too~ You’ll need them for what comes next~’

And so Filo-tan’s voice gradually grew more distant until it faded entirely. I tried to chase after it, but it was as if I’d hit a wall, unable to move any further. Literally, there was an invisible wall standing in front of the door, indeed.
“Ahh, Filo-taaaan!”
And so, in this world, the voice of Filo-tan — who here was Sakura-chan — could no longer be heard, indeed.
